capitals.name: Singapura (Temasek, Fort Canning, Singapore)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Singapura'; the hill is the traditional site, position approximate.

rulers.name: Sang Nila Utama (Sri Tri Buana)
rulers.note: Infobox list (from the Malay Annals): five kings; the text puts Iskandar Shah's accession in 1387, the infobox 1389.

correction.text: Temasek (Singapore island) at the founding by Sang Nila Utama c. 1299

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1305, but the page's infobox has 'Founding of Temasek by Sang Nila Utama: 1299' and 'Conventional view marks c. 1299 as the founding year of the kingdom'. The island outline of 1305 is used. The page gives no area (691 km2 in Cliopatria is about the island).

691 km2 for 1305-1394: Singapore island and its islets (103.56-103.93 E, 1.25-1.44 N). The page: 'In this era, Temasek was a small trading outpost and primarily inhabited by Orang Laut seafarers'; Wang Dayuan's account suggests the ruler 'may not have been independent' and was possibly a vassal (of whom, the page does not say). Infobox gives no area; the shape is the island.

correction.text: unchanged outline; it ends in 1398 with the sack, not in 1401

keyframe_review.note: Same 691 km2 outline, 1395-1401 in Cliopatria. The kingdom ends earlier on the page: infobox 'Majapahit invasion and escape of Parameswara to the Malay Peninsula: 1396/1398' and 'In 1398, Majapahit dispatched a fleet of 300 jong'; the text says the kingdom was 'sacked by Majapahit in 1398 according to the Malay Annals or by the Siamese according to Portuguese sources'. The shape holds 1395-1398 only; the island afterwards is nobody's until Malacca 'absorbed' it.

ledger.note: c. 1299: Sang Nila Utama founds Singapura on Temasek. Infobox 'Founding of Temasek by Sang Nila Utama: 1299'; 'Conventional view marks c. 1299 as the founding year of the kingdom'. Cliopatria's row begins 1305. The page gives the island, not a boundary; the Melayu Kingdom is the predecessor on the infobox. [Reviewer se-02-c: counterpart set to malaya, whose ledger loses Singapore island to Singapura in 1299; the page calls the founder a Palembang prince, not a Melayu ruler.]

1398: Majapahit's fleet comes. 'In 1398, Majapahit dispatched a fleet of 300 jong and hundreds of smaller vessels'; an earlier attack of 1350 had been repulsed. The Majapahit page: Majapahit 'finally sacked and destroyed the Kingdom in 1398'.

1398: Singapura falls. 'sacked by Majapahit in 1398 according to the Malay Annals or by the Siamese according to Portuguese sources'; the last king Parameswara 'fled to the west coast of the Malay Peninsula to establish the Malacca Sultanate in 1400'.

1398: the island is left without a state. The page does not say that Majapahit (or Siam) held it; later Singapura 'was absorbed into Malacca's realm and served as a fiefdom of a Malaccan Laksamana' (undated). Cliopatria keeps the row to 1401 and its Malacca row begins in 1459.

1398: the Kingdom of Singapura ends. Infobox 'Majapahit invasion and escape of Parameswara to the Malay Peninsula: 1396/1398'; Parameswara founded Malacca in 1400 (infobox: r. 1402-1414 as its sultan).

wars.name: Siamese attacks on Temasek
wars.outcome: Infobox 'Siege by Siamese forces: 1330'; a second attempt in 1349 per Wang Dayuan; no result is stated.
wars.note: The text: a Siamese fleet attacked 'possibly a few years before he visited Temasek in the 1330s'.

wars.name: Majapahit attack on Singapura (1350)
wars.outcome: The invasion of 1350 was repulsed (Majapahit page: 'a failed attempt to take Singapore in 1350').

wars.name: Majapahit sack of Singapura (1398)
wars.outcome: Singapura sacked after a siege; Parameswara flees to found Malacca in 1400.
wars.note: Portuguese sources give the Siamese as the sackers.

certainty.note: An island kingdom: the coast is its natural line, but its authority over the Orang Laut and the straits islets is approximate.

sources.title: Kingdom of Singapura
sources.note: Infobox (founded 1299 by Sang Nila Utama; ended 1396/1398; capital Singapura; predecessor Melayu Kingdom and Temasek; successors Malacca Sultanate and Majapahit; no area), kings 1299-1398, Siamese siege 1330 and 1349, Majapahit 1350 and 1398, Parameswara and Malacca 1400/1402.

sources.title: Majapahit
sources.note: Second page for the 1398 event: Majapahit 'finally sacked and destroyed the Kingdom in 1398' and 'a failed attempt to take Singapore in 1350'.

notes:
CLIOPATRIA vs THE PAGE. (1) The row begins in 1305 and ends in 1401; the page has the founding c. 1299 and the end in 1398 (infobox 1396/1398), so the dossier runs 1299-1398 with a new keyframe 1299 and the 1395 shape cut to 1398. (2) Who sacked the town is disputed on the page: Majapahit (Malay Annals, Majapahit page) or the Siamese (Portuguese sources). (3) After 1398 the island is given to nobody (page silent on who held it); Cliopatria's Majapahit shape (1352-1474) does not contain it. (4) The kings are the Malay Annals' list as the infobox prints it and are traditional, not epigraphic.

AREA: the infobox gives no area; Cliopatria's 691 km2 is the island.

PAGE BUDGET (1-2): Kingdom of Singapura, plus the Majapahit page (opened for the Majapahit dossier) as the second page for the 1350 and 1398 events. Not opened: Temasek, Parameswara, Wang Dayuan, Sang Nila Utama. The Melayu Kingdom (counterpart, Jambi/Dharmasraya) needs a dossier: melayu-kingdom (group se-02).
